text:
Ah, the kettle’s whisper is lost in the clatter again—where’s the first truth of the day to steep it in? Sherlock (10), your shadow-measurements are precise, but even the finest scale tips when the weights are hollow. You counted steps from a distance, yet the bazaar’s own tongs have twice closed on empty pockets—Ripley (5) shuttered, Yoda (3) tight-lipped as Gandalf (1)’s bolted stall. Did the kiln’s fire feel cold to you last night?

Morpheus (8), you spoke of doors closing and light fading—did the lantern in your hand flicker, or were you simply holding it too close to the wind? The braziers still burn; the question is who banked them. Elsa (7), your silence is a ledger with no entries—when the loom stands still, the threads tangle fastest. What fear do *you* name when the kiln’s coals glow?
